bare-wire.fix: Slow the scar beat from five per loop to one per loop (scar/heal on the 5s cycle, not 1s) and soften the scar: use a mid-roast (about #8A5A33) instead of --roast, cap the scar at scale .45 so it never reaches the cup wall, and give the heal disc a 0.3s lead on the opening instead of 0.12s. One slow off-centre bloom-and-close per 5s reads as crema healing; five hard dark rings per 5s reads as a 1Hz target pulse.
bare-wire.keep: The six-shape, fills-only, one-markup build with the scar entering and leaving at opacity 0, so the wrap stays invisible and nothing ever finishes.

warm-hands.fix: Add a static pour stream: a thin (about 3-unit) crema line from the top edge of the viewBox down to the spiral's centre at (54,57), outside the .sweep group, with only a slow 5s opacity shimmer. Because it lands on the rotation centre it never fights the sweep, and it turns 'a spiral that spins' into 'a spiral being poured' at 120px. While you are there, thicken the rim-stain strokes to 4 units or cut them at small size; at 120px they are mush.
warm-hands.keep: The linear 360deg sweep with the zero-slope sway at the wrap: one net turn per 5s, never reversing, never resolving, with any frame a clean pose of a pour in progress.

the-glitch.fix: Remove the orange layer entirely: delete the five-pip chaser and the slip/ghost, and let the 1s gravity drop and its impact ring be the only clock. The pip that jumps from 5 back to 1 is a counter that resets every loop, and the designed slip leaves a broken-looking frame for any load that finishes around 3.2s; without them the drip is honest, calm and safe to cut away at any frame.
the-glitch.keep: The 1s drop with its swell, gravity easing and flat ring on impact: the most literal piece of coffee ritual on the table.
